transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, so what finally scared me into coming in today is that I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work. I work in video production and editing, and I know better than to make the errors I'm making. 

Lately, I've been doing things like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note from a producer. I even exported a client cut recently with the wrong lower-third graphic on it, and that was after I had already checked it. It's just getting really frustrating, and it's starting to affect my work, so I needed to come in and figure out what's going on.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness or difficulty focusing your entire life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

It's... well, it's been my entire life, honestly. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers actually had to move my desk a lot. I was always getting out of my seat, or I'd be blurting out answers, or just bothering my classmates before I even realized I was doing it. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me.

Looking back at your childhood, would you say that your difficulties with sitting still or impulsivity were just as prominent as your struggles with focus and organization, or was the restlessness more of a background issue compared to the inattention?

Um, I think the restlessness was definitely just as prominent. Honestly, it might have been the most obvious thing about me back then. 

The focus stuff was definitely there—I struggled with that too—but the not sitting still and the blurting things out... that was definitely front and center. It wasn't in the background at all, mostly because that was usually the stuff that actually got me in trouble with the teachers.
Looking at your life today, do you still feel that sense of physical restlessness or an urge to act impulsively, or has that part of your experience faded compared to when you were a child?

It definitely hasn't faded. I still feel it pretty often today. Um, like, if I have to sit still through a client screening, it honestly feels like there's this pressure building up under my skin. I just get this really strong urge where I feel like I need to get up and do something with my body... even when I know perfectly well that I'm supposed to just sit there and watch the cut quietly. So, yeah, the physical restlessness is still very much there.

Beyond the physical restlessness and impulsivity you described, would you say that you currently struggle significantly with being easily distracted by external stimuli or losing track of tasks in your daily life?

Um, not really, no. I don't think I struggle with that part very much. Like, when I'm editing a video or working behind the camera, I can usually stay on track with what I'm doing. I don't really get pulled away by things happening around me, and I don't usually lose track of my tasks. 

It's really just... the physical part, you know? The needing to move. But my actual focus on the work itself is usually fine. I haven't really noticed distraction being a big issue for me.
In your current day-to-day life, do you find that you frequently interrupt others while they are speaking or finish their sentences before they have a chance to?

Yeah, I do that a lot, actually. I catch myself cutting into other people's conversations all the time. Or, like, at work, I'll find myself leaning right over an assistant's shoulder to fix something on their timeline before they've even asked me for help. I know it comes off like I don't trust them, but I just... I see it and I just jump in before I can stop myself.
Outside of your work, do you find that you frequently lose important items or struggle to keep your personal schedule and daily chores organized?

No, not really. I don't usually lose things like my keys or my phone, and I'm pretty okay at keeping my personal life organized. I mean, I pay my bills on time and get my chores done. I don't really struggle with that kind of stuff. It's just the feeling like I have a motor running inside me all the time that's the problem.
